Cc: EdgeSight Procurement <procure@edgesight.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tiered availability compression proposal & pilot pricing

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — great to learn more about EdgeSight's mobile inference use case and the seasonality you mentioned for Q2. Attached is a concise draft that compresses our usual uptime/response bands into a simpler, two-line commercial with an option for a short pilot. High-level:

- Compression option A (Standard): 99.5% uptime, 4 hr response, price = baseline + per-token usage.
- Compression option B (Assured): 99.95% uptime, 1 hr response, includes escalation coverage and monthly reliability review; priced as a blended commit.

We also included an optional 6-week pilot template that lowers the SLA to 99.0% with a fixed usage cap and a buyout credit if you convert to a committed term. That pilot path often helps procurement move faster.

Attachments: SLA_Tiers_v1.pdf, pilot-commit-template.docx

If you can share the expected steady-state token throughput and any mandated procurement terms, I can run numbers for a 6- and 12-month commit and propose a discount band.

Would you be available for a 20-min call on Thursday to walk through the pilot assumptions?

Best,

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0137

Kim,

Appreciate the clear summary and the pilot path — that could be the fastest route for us. A few clarifying questions before we hop on a call:

1) For the Assured band, does "escalation coverage" include named on-call contacts during business hours and an escalation engineer outside of business hours? We need coverage beyond our standard support windows.
2) Can you confirm what counts as "per-token" usage for billing — are you counting user-visible tokens only, or do internal system tokens (parsing, reranking) count?
3) About the buyout credit on pilot conversion: how is the credit calculated and applied to the committed term?

Procurement also asked whether you can provide a one-time goodwill discount if we commit to 12 months at an 18-month effective runway (i.e., a 12-mo contract with a 6-mo renewal option that we can exercise early).

If you can sketch answers in an email we can iterate quickly. Prefer to keep the Thursday slot open for a working session if needed.

Kim / Aisha — quick answers from ops and commercial: 

1) Escalation coverage: For the Assured band we can commit to a named SME during ramp (first 30 days) and provide 24/7 escalation for Sev1 incidents with an SLO of 60 minutes to engage an on-call engineer. Outside of Sev1, business-hours escalation applies. We should avoid committing to a guaranteed engineer on-site; keep remote escalation and escalation bridge coverage.

2) Token counting: We bill on final user-visible tokens. Internal system tokens (reranks, parsing helpers) are not billed in the per-token charge; however, for heavy reranking workflows we recommend a separate inference bundle to avoid noise on usage.

3) Pilot buyout credit: propose this formula — if pilot converts to a 12-month commit within 30 days of pilot end, credit = min(pilot_fees, 0.2 * first_year_commit_value). That gives procurement something meaningful while limiting our downside.

4) One-time goodwill discount: commercial okays a 7% one-time credit applied against the first invoice for a 12-month commit with the 6-month early-exercise clause. If they want higher, require a 6+ month minimum committed usage ramp and a signature from legal on a no-refund clause for early exit.

I recommend we present the pilot + buyout credit and the one-time 7% as the initial offer. Leaves room to upsell additional escalation hours as an add-on.

Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Offers
Redwood Inference

Kim,

Thanks — that set of answers is really helpful and gives procurement enough to proceed. We like the pilot + 0.2 cap credit approach and the commitment-friendly 7% goodwill credit. Two follow-ups from procurement side:

- Can we get the 7% applied as a pre-invoice credit rather than applied to the first invoice after payment? It helps our cashflow modeling.
- For the Assured band, can the 60-minute engagement SLO be described as an "acknowledgement & escalation bridge established within 60 minutes" to ensure SREs on our side have time to assemble?

If you're able to adjust the language, procurement will route this to legal and we can sign the pilot SOW quickly. Assuming legal is OK, we plan to run the 6-week pilot starting March 2.

Would you send a short one-page amendment to the pilot template with these two language tweaks and the discount mechanics? If possible, include a DocuSign link for faster turnaround.

Best,
